newsitem.title: USA: Illinois corn, soybean harvests slowly advance.
newsitem.headline: Illinois corn, soybean harvests slowly advance.

text.p: Illinois' corn and soybean harvests were in their early stages during the week ended Sunday, with corn four percent harvested and soybeans one percent, according to the Illinois Agricultural Statistics Service weekly crop update.
Last year, six percent of the corn had been cut and three of the soybeans while the average for corn was 13 percent and soybeans 12 percent.

Rain in the southern areas aided soybeans with slight improvement evident in the condition ratings. Soybeans were rated four percent excellent, 33 good, 42 fair, 15 poor and six very poor, versus four, 41, 41, 18 and six, respectively, a week ago.
Corn was rated six percent excellent, 47 percent good, 32 fair, 11 poor and four percent very poor.
Sorghum was one percent harvested and 30 mature, versus none a week ago and 14 percent a year ago, respectively, and seven and 44 for the averages.
Topsoil moisture was rated 16 percent very short, 47 percent short, 37 percent adequate and nil surplus, the report said.
